💡 This work pioneers particle-level mechanical reinforcement of Ni-rich cathodes, achieving a fivefold crushing-strength increase and reduced stress accumulation, which suppresses fracture during high-voltage cycling. 💡 Sulfonated TiO₂ nanorods actively promote LiTFSI dissociation via Lewis base sites, unlike passive fillers. Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 reconstructs Li-rich layered oxide surfaces into a cation-disordered, fluorine-incorporating subsurface layer, passivating the oxidative interface and eliminating cathode–solid electrolyte degradation. This enables ~300.3 mAh g–1 capacity and 82.3% retention over 1500 cycles in all-solid-state batteries, and the strategy extends to Ni-rich oxides, offering a universal interfacial design route for high-energy ASSBs.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work introduces the first sulfonimide-based polymer of intrinsic microporosity (FAS-PIM) and directly compares it with flexible, non-microporous polysulfonimide analogs. Adding succinonitrile drives both architectures toward similar conductivity, thermomechanical properties, and reprocessability, despite differing conduction mechanisms. This establishes convergence between permanently microporous and transiently porous single-ion conducting electrolytes, offering design guidance for next-generation materials.
